passageList.quote: During the Proto-Urban Garamantian phase (PUGAR), 500 BC-1 BC, what was to become the capital of the Garamantes, Garama, was established

the Garamantes can be seen as an early desert state … The Garamantian civilisation, from the earliest phase, between 1000-500 BC, and the 5 th -6 th centuries AD, has seen the development of agriculture and urbanism together with the rise of a hierarchical society

Despite being defeated by Roman armies - notably Cornelius Balbus, proconsul of Africa (20 BC), as described by Pliny ( Natural History V 35-37) … the Garamantes were never annexed to the Roman Empire.

The Wadi al-Ajal, where the capital Garama is located, became the centre of this civilisation that extended to the Wadi Tanezzuft on the west, the Wadi ash-Shati to the north and the Zuwila-Murzuq-Barjuj depression
